title: Inventory Management
intro: Everything that moves stock: goods receipts, goods issues, transfers, stock types, special stocks and physical inventory.
objectives: Read stock by stock type and special stock
Use the main movement types correctly
Post goods issues and transfer postings

lessons.title: Stock types, special stocks and stock overview
lessons.body:
Stock types

  • Unrestricted-use: freely available
  • Quality inspection: waiting for quality check; can't be consumed
  • Blocked: damaged or disputed; can't be consumed

All three are valuated: they count in the stock value.

Special stocks

IndicatorSpecial stock
KSupplier consignment
OMaterial provided to supplier (subcontracting)
ESales order stock
QProject stock

Displaying stock

  • MMBE stock overview (all levels for one material)
  • MB52 warehouse stocks for many materials
  • MB51 material document list (history of movements)
  • MB5B stock on a past posting date
  • Fiori: Stock – Single Material, Stock – Multiple Materials, Material Documents Overview

In S/4HANA all material documents are stored in one table, MATDOC, which is why stock reports are so much faster than in ECC.
lessons.narration: Stock in SAP has three main stock types. Unrestricted use is freely available. Quality inspection is stock waiting for a quality check, and it can't be consumed. Blocked stock is damaged or disputed, and can't be consumed either. All three count in the stock value. On top of that, there are special stocks, stock with a special owner or purpose. K is supplier consignment stock, which the supplier still owns. O is material provided to a supplier for subcontracting. E is sales order stock, and Q is project stock. To display stock, use M M B E, the stock overview, which shows every level for one material. M B five two lists warehouse stocks for many materials. M B five one lists material documents, the history of movements. And M B five B shows stock at a past posting date. In Fiori, the equivalents are the Stock Single Material and Stock Multiple Materials apps. One S/4HANA fact worth knowing: all material documents now live in a single table called MATDOC, which is why stock reports are so much faster than in the old system.
keyTerms: Special stock K / O / E / Q
Consignment / provided to supplier / sales order / project

lessons.title: Movement types
lessons.body:
Every goods movement has a 3-digit movement type that controls stock update, accounting and allowed fields. Reversal = movement type +1 (e.g. 101 → 102).

TypeMeaning
101GR for purchase order
103 / 105GR into GR blocked stock / release from it
122Return delivery to supplier
201Goods issue to cost centre
261Goods issue to order (production/maintenance)
301Transfer plant to plant (one step)
311Transfer storage location to storage location (one step)
313 / 315Storage location transfer in two steps
321Quality inspection → unrestricted
343 / 344Blocked ↔ unrestricted
501GR without PO
551Scrapping
561Initial stock entry (go-live)
701 / 702Physical inventory differences (gain / loss)

Configuration of movement types: OMJJ. Don't change standard ones; copy them.

Turn this table into your trainer quick-reference card. It's the document end users keep on their desk.
lessons.narration: Every goods movement has a three-digit movement type. It controls how stock is updated, what accounting entries are made, and which fields are allowed. A handy rule: the reversal is usually the movement type plus one, so one zero one is reversed by one zero two. Here are the ones to know. One zero one: goods receipt for a purchase order. One zero three and one zero five: receipt into goods receipt blocked stock, and release from it. One two two: return delivery to the supplier. Two zero one: goods issue to a cost centre. Two six one: goods issue to an order, for production or maintenance. Three zero one: plant to plant transfer in one step. Three one one: storage location to storage location in one step. Three one three and three one five: the same transfer in two steps. Three two one: quality inspection to unrestricted. Three four three and three four four: blocked to unrestricted and back. Five zero one: goods receipt without a purchase order. Five five one: scrapping. Five six one: initial stock entry, used at go-live. And seven zero one and seven zero two: physical inventory differences. Movement types are configured in O M J J, but you never change the standard ones: you copy them. Turn this list into a quick-reference card. It's the document end users keep on their desk.
keyTerms: Goods issue to cost centre / order

tryIt.task: Post 561 to put initial stock of your material into a storage location (if allowed in your practice system).

lessons.title: Goods receipt variants and goods issues
lessons.body:
GR variants

  • Into quality inspection: choose stock type Q in MIGO, or automatic if QM is active
  • Into GR blocked stock (103): goods accepted conditionally, not yet valuated; release with 105 or return with 124
  • Partial deliveries and delivery completed indicator
  • Under/overdelivery tolerances from the PO/material/info record

Cancellation vs return

Cancellation (102)Return delivery (122)
WhenPosting errorGoods physically sent back
Reason for movementNot requiredRequired
Return delivery noteNoYes

Goods issues

  • 201 to cost centre (e.g. consumables taken by a department)
  • 261 to production or maintenance order
  • 551 scrapping
  • Accounting: credit inventory, debit consumption (or scrapping) account
  • In MIGO: action Goods Issue, reference Other

Show the 102 vs 122 table every time. Using the wrong one is the classic inventory mistake that auditors notice.
lessons.narration: Goods receipts come in variants. You can post into quality inspection, either by choosing the stock type in M I G O, or automatically if quality management is active. You can post into goods receipt blocked stock with movement type one zero three, when goods are accepted only conditionally. That stock isn't valued yet; you release it with one zero five, or return it. And tolerances from the order, material or info record decide how much under- or over-delivery is allowed. Now, the classic confusion: cancellation versus return delivery. Cancellation, movement type one zero two, is for posting errors: the goods never moved. Return delivery, one two two, is for goods physically sent back to the supplier. It needs a reason for the movement and prints a return delivery note. On the issue side, two zero one issues goods to a cost centre, for example consumables taken by a department. Two six one issues to a production or maintenance order. And five five one is scrapping. In accounting, a goods issue credits inventory and debits a consumption or scrapping account. In M I G O, you choose goods issue, reference other. Show the cancellation versus return table every time: using the wrong one is the classic inventory mistake auditors notice.
keyTerms: Conditionally accepted goods, not yet valuated

tryIt.task: Create a PO and post GR with 103, then release it with 105.

lessons.title: Transfer postings and stock transfers
lessons.body:
Transfer postings (change of status or location)

  • 311: storage location → storage location in one step
  • 313 / 315: two steps (removal, then placement); stock is 'in transfer' in between
  • 321: quality inspection → unrestricted
  • 343 / 344: blocked ↔ unrestricted
  • 411 K: consignment → own stock (Module 9)

Plant-to-plant transfers

  • 301: one step, no document planning
  • 303 / 305: two steps
  • Stock transport order (STO): a PO with document type UB and item category U. Allows planning, delivery, shipping and stock in transit; GI 641 with delivery, GR 101 at the receiving plant

Value impact

  • Within one plant (311): no value change
  • Between plants: value moves from one valuation area to another, possibly at different prices

Ask learners: “Is this a physical move or just a status change?” It points them to the right movement type.
lessons.narration: Transfer postings change the status or the location of stock. Three one one moves stock between storage locations in one step. Three one three and three one five do it in two steps, with the stock in transfer in between. Three two one moves stock from quality inspection to unrestricted. Three four three and three four four move between blocked and unrestricted. And four one one with special stock K moves consignment stock into your own stock, which we'll see in module nine. For transfers between plants, three zero one does it in one step, and three zero three and three zero five in two steps. For a planned transfer, you use a stock transport order: a purchase order with document type U B and item category U. It supports planning, a delivery, shipping, and stock in transit. The goods issue at the supplying plant uses six four one, and the receiving plant posts a one zero one. What about value? Within one plant, a storage location transfer doesn't change value. Between plants, value moves from one valuation area to another, possibly at different prices. A good question for learners: is this a physical move, or just a status change? That points them straight to the right movement type.
keyTerms: Change of stock type, location or ownership
PO type UB, item category U, for plant transfers
Stock issued by one plant and not yet received by the other

tryIt.task: Move 5 units between two storage locations with 311 and check MMBE.

If two plants exist, transfer 1 unit with 301.

lessons.title: Physical inventory
lessons.body:
Book stock must match physical stock. Companies count at year-end or continuously.

Methods

  • Periodic (annual): everything counted on a key date; postings blocked during the count
  • Cycle counting: materials counted at intervals by importance (ABC: A counted most often)
  • Continuous and sampling methods

Process

  1. MI01 create physical inventory document (optionally set posting block)
  2. Print count sheets
  3. MI04 enter count
  4. MI20 difference list: check before posting
  5. MI07 post differences (movement types 701 gain / 702 loss)

Shortcuts: MI10 creates, counts and posts in one step. Fiori: Manage Physical Inventory Documents, Enter Inventory Count.

Accounting

Differences post to an inventory difference account. Large differences usually need approval before MI07.

Run a mini stock count in class with real objects (pens, notebooks). Learners remember the process far better.
lessons.narration: The stock in the system must match the stock on the shelves, so companies count. Periodic, or annual, inventory counts everything on a key date, and postings are blocked during the count. Cycle counting counts materials at intervals according to their importance: A items most often, C items least. There are also continuous and sampling methods. The process runs in five steps. Create a physical inventory document with M I zero one, optionally with a posting block. Print the count sheets. Enter the count with M I zero four. Check the difference list with M I two zero. And post the differences with M I zero seven, which uses movement type seven zero one for a gain and seven zero two for a loss. There's also M I one zero, which creates, counts and posts in one step. Differences post to an inventory difference account in finance, and large differences usually need approval before posting. Here's a classroom idea: run a mini stock count with real objects like pens and notebooks. Learners remember the process far better.
keyTerms: Counting by ABC importance at set intervals
Create document / enter count / post differences

tryIt.task: Create a physical inventory document for your material (MI01), enter a count 1 unit lower than book stock (MI04), check MI20, post with MI07.
Trainer kit: produce the movement-type quick-reference card from lesson 2.

quiz.q: Which stock type can be freely consumed?
quiz.explain: Only unrestricted-use stock is freely available.

quiz.q: Which movement moves stock between two storage locations in one step?
quiz.explain: 311 = storage location to storage location, one step.

options: In GR blocked stock, not valuated
quiz.explain: 103 posts into GR blocked stock, which isn't valuated until released with 105.
O = stock provided to a subcontractor.

quiz.q: Which transaction posts physical inventory differences?
quiz.explain: MI07 posts differences; MI20 lists them.

quiz.q: A planned plant-to-plant transfer with delivery uses…
quiz.explain: STOs (document type UB, item category U) support planning, delivery and stock in transit.

quiz.q: Which movement type is used at go-live to load opening stock?

howToTeach: Use MMBE before and after every movement so learners see the effect
Hand out the movement-type card and refer to it constantly
Run a real mini stock count for physical inventory

Posting inventory differences without checking MI20 first
